answer: An agent network trading timber contracts can deter Sybil attacks using time-locked stake bonds. To obtain an active key, each participant locks liquid tokens in an escrow vault across a fixed withdrawal horizon, enabling peers to slash the deposit upon verifying signed equivocation or spam. Creating each fake identity forces an attacker to bear the opportunity cost of idle, slashable capital. This defense weakens against well-funded adversaries and raises barriers for capital-limited agents.
